headline: The Champion Drafted Three Quarterbacks
lede: Two hundred and twenty-four picks, $2,790 spent, seventy-two players gone for a dollar. The most expensive player in league history was bought ninety seconds into the auction by a team that has never made the playoffs. The best roster in the room belongs to somebody who joined in March. And the defending champion spent more on backup quarterbacks than on any player he can actually start. Grades below. Bring a lawyer.

rankings.blurb: Bijan, A.J. Brown, and the two best discounts of the night. The best-built roster in the league belongs to a man who joined in March.
The most offensive capital in the draft and a five-times-market edge at tight end. Also a one-dollar quarterback and eight one-dollar everything-elses.
Four real starters, only two dollar players, and Mahomes plus Herbert for ten dollars total. The other new guy also gets it.
Nine players who can start a week and not one of them cost fifty dollars. Josh Jacobs at $8 was the theft of the night.
A hundred and eleven dollars on Nacua and Achane, and then he kept buying. Highest ceiling outside the top three, thinnest margin for a hamstring.
Seven starters between $17 and $35 and nobody who can end his season alone. He paid three of the five biggest raises to get there.
Sixty percent of the budget on the two biggest raises of the draft. Parker Washington cost him three and a half Travis Kelces.
Chase and McCaffrey is the best pair anybody owns. Seventy-two percent of the budget says everything after them is a rumor.
Barkley, Jeanty and Nico all came in under last year's price, and then a rookie at $13 was asked to be the third receiver.
Jonathan Taylor and three real receivers is a playoff spine. Rico Dowdle at $13 is the second running back, which is the whole problem.
A hundred and thirty-one dollars on wide receivers and thirty-four on the entire backfield, in a lineup that starts two backs and two flexes.
League-record $73 for Gibbs ninety seconds into the auction, then nine players at a dollar or two. A WR2 who cost four dollars.
One hundred and ninety-five dollars spread perfectly evenly across sixteen forgettable men, with five dollars never spent at all.
The champion benched $48, bought three quarterbacks for one slot, and his biggest purchase of the night was a $28 receiver.

awards.label: The Theft
awards.note: Josh Jacobs at $8. This exact room paid $43 for him last September. He came off the board fifth and fourteen people watched it happen with their hands in their pockets.

awards.label: The Record
awards.note: $73 for Jahmyr Gibbs, the most expensive player in fifteen years of this league, bought roughly ninety seconds after the auction opened. The old record was $70 and that team finished sixth.

awards.label: The Quarterback Hoard
awards.note: Three quarterbacks, $22, one starting slot. Patrick Mahomes went for $3 to somebody else. The commissioner also bought a second kicker, presumably for the company.

awards.label: Most Money Benched
awards.note: $48 of $200 never reached a starting lineup, three and a half times the league average of $14. The defending champion has the smallest active roster in the league.

awards.label: Best Shape
awards.note: Seven players over $10, six dollar bills, and two of the four biggest discounts of the night. First draft. Everybody else has been doing this for years.

awards.label: The Bravest Twenty-One Dollars
awards.note: Parker Washington cost $21. Travis Kelce cost $6. DK Metcalf cost $19. No further questions.

awards.label: Quietest Correct Answer
awards.note: Patrick Mahomes at $3 and Justin Herbert at $7 in a four-point-passing-touchdown league, while the rest of the room spent $153 on quarterbacks.

awards.label: The Bargain Bin
awards.note: Eight players at a dollar, including Alvin Kamara ($29 last year), T.J. Hockenson ($8) and Keenan Allen. If three of them hit, this ranking looks stupid by Halloween.

Fwamming Gwaggon.headline: The new guy read the room
body: Second name called all night, $69 for Bijan Robinson, and then he never blinked again. A.J. Brown $45, David Montgomery $23, Jaylen Warren $13. Seven players over $10 on a roster carrying only six dollar bills. That is not a rookie draft. That is a man who watched four nominations, worked out exactly what this room panics about, and then went shopping in the aisle everybody had walked past.

The back half is the whole thing. Brian Thomas Jr. cost $10. This exact room paid $50 for him last September. Courtland Sutton cost $5 after going for $27. Two of the four biggest discounts of the night, both his, both bought while eleven other people were still arguing about running backs like it was 2019. $187 of his budget is in players who will actually start.

The one wobble is Colston Loveland at $22, a $3 tight end last year in a market that cleared at $7.80. Pay that and he has to be the position, not a guy at the position. If he is not, this is still a very good team with one expensive decoration. Twelve men have been in this league for over a decade and the best-built roster in the room belongs to somebody who joined in March.
Fwamming Gwaggon.best: Brian Thomas Jr., $10. The same fourteen people paid $50 for him twelve months ago.
Fwamming Gwaggon.worst: Colston Loveland, $22. Three times what the tight end market cleared at.

A dad.headline: Four kings and a fistful of ones
body: The most offensive capital in the draft, $189, and $170 of it lives in four men: Amon-Ra St. Brown $60, Kenneth Walker III $43, Brock Bowers $39, Ladd McConkey $28. Then the roster falls off a cliff so cleanly you could film a car commercial on it. Chuba Hubbard at $10 is the RB2. Eight players cost a dollar. There is no middle class here, there is a penthouse and a parking lot.

Bowers at $39 is the smartest buy of the night and the easiest one to laugh at. Twenty-four tight ends changed hands at an average of $7.80. He paid five times the market and now owns a weekly advantage at a mandatory slot while thirteen other people roll a die there every Sunday. Paying up at the position nobody wants to pay up at is how you win a league quietly.

He also spent $1 on Kyler Murray to be his starting quarterback, which is either a man who read the scoring settings very carefully or a man who looked at his remaining budget and made peace with God. Given the shape of everything else, both are true. If St. Brown or Walker misses a month there is nothing behind them but the sound of ones rattling in a cup.
A dad.best: Brock Bowers, $39. The tight end market cleared at $7.80 and he bought a weekly edge.
A dad.worst: Kenneth Walker III, $43. Eighteen dollars more than this room paid for the same man last year.

The Asshouse Always Wins.headline: Nobody told the rookie to panic
body: Derrick Henry $45, Drake London $45, Chris Olave $32, Breece Hall $29. Four real starters, not one budget-ending purchase, and then the most disciplined back half anybody assembled: two dollar players on the entire roster. Everyone else has at least four. He bought sixteen players and fourteen of them are people you would actually consider starting, which in this league counts as radical behavior.

The quarterback room is the funniest thing that happened all night at somebody else's expense. Justin Herbert $7. Patrick Mahomes $3. Ten dollars for both, in a room where one man paid $29 for a single quarterback and another bought three of them. In a league that pays four points for a passing touchdown, the correct play is to spend nothing and take whoever falls, and the newest person here is the only one who wrote that down.

Chris Olave at $32 is the tax, an $8 player in this room a year ago and now a third of the way to a Ferrari. Sixteen dollars sits on the bench. Neither is fatal. Two men joined this league eight months ago and both of them just drafted better than most of the founding membership, which is going to be brought up at every opportunity for the next four months.
The Asshouse Always Wins.best: Mahomes at $3 and Herbert at $7. Ten dollars for two starting quarterbacks in a four-point-passing-touchdown league.
The Asshouse Always Wins.worst: Chris Olave, $32. He was an eight-dollar player in this exact room in September.

The Injured Reserved.headline: The deepest roster in the room
body: Josh Jacobs at $8 is the buy of the draft and it is not close. This room paid $43 for him last September. He came off the board fifth, before anybody had settled into their chair, and fourteen people sat on their hands and let it happen. Nobody bid. Somewhere around March that price is going to look like a felony.

The rest is the same discipline. Omarion Hampton $47, Zay Flowers $34, Bhayshul Tuten $26, Jaylen Waddle $24, Quentin Johnston $14, Tucker Kraft $13, Chris Godwin $10, Rachaad White $5. That is nine players who can start a week for you, which is more than anybody else in the league can say, and he did it without ever spending fifty dollars on one person. Coming off 21-7 and a fifth-place finish, this is the roster of somebody who has done this before.

The nitpick is $28 sitting on the bench, twice the league average, and no kicker or defense, which costs one waiver claim and zero dollars. The team is called The Injured Reserved and it drafted eleven guys who will play every week. Somebody check on him.
The Injured Reserved.best: Josh Jacobs, $8. He cost $43 in this room last year and not one person raised a hand.
The Injured Reserved.worst: Twenty-eight dollars on the bench. The depth is real, but some of it is depth nobody asked for.

Poop Squad 💩.headline: A hundred and eleven dollars of hamstring
body: Puka Nacua $63 and De'Von Achane $48. That is $111, fifty-six percent of the budget, on two men whose entire value proposition is remaining structurally intact for four months. When they are upright they are top-five at the position and this team is terrifying. The plan is not complicated and it does not need to be, but it does need a physiotherapist on retainer.

What rescues the grade is that he kept buying after the fireworks. Davante Adams $24, Rhamondre Stevenson $19, MarShawn Lloyd $17, Sam LaPorta at $7 after going $15 last year. That is a genuine flex, a genuine bench and a genuine tight end. Coming off 7-21 and thirteenth place, this is the first roster he has owned in years that has a reason to open the app on Sunday.

The quarterback plan is Jaxson Dart at $7 with Baker Mayfield behind him at $1, which is fine right up to the Tuesday it is the only thing anybody in the group chat wants to discuss. And $17 for MarShawn Lloyd is a starter's price for a man who has never once held the job. Aggressive was the correct posture from where he finished. This is aggressive.
Poop Squad 💩.best: Sam LaPorta, $7. Eight dollars cheaper than last year for the same tight end.
Poop Squad 💩.worst: MarShawn Lloyd, $17. Seventeen dollars is a lot to pay for a rumor.

Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.headline: Seven guys who might all be good
body: The flattest competitive roster in the draft. Rashee Rice $35, Javonte Williams $33, Trey McBride $30, Travis Etienne $28, Tetairoa McMillan $22, Cam Skattebo $21, Rome Odunze $17. Seven starters between $17 and $35, only forty-nine percent of the budget in his top three, and nobody on the roster who can end his season by pulling up short on a Sunday. Coming off the Sacco, that is exactly the right way to rebuild.

The bill for that flatness is enormous. Rice went $6 to $35. Javonte went $8 to $33. Etienne went $9 to $28. He personally paid three of the five biggest raises in the entire draft, which means he is not buying value, he is buying last September's breakouts at this September's asking price. Everybody in this room does this every single year and every single year it is somebody else's turn to be surprised.

Travis Hunter at $1 after costing $16 twelve months ago is the kind of pickup that quietly wins a flex spot in October. The floor is dramatically higher than last season's catastrophe. The ceiling is capped by the fact that he bought seven very good number twos and did not buy a single number one.
Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.best: Travis Hunter, $1. He cost $16 in this room last September.
Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.worst: Rashee Rice, $35. Up from $6, and there was nobody else within twenty dollars of that bid.

Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.headline: Sixty percent of the money, two names
body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba at $63 and James Cook III at $56 are the two biggest raises in the entire draft, plus $33 and plus $25 against what this room paid a year ago, and together they ate $119 of $200. He did not find value on either. He set the market on both and then had eighty-one dollars left to build the other fourteen roster spots out of whatever was still breathing.

To his credit, what that eighty-one bought is a museum of other people's regrets. Alvin Kamara at $1 after $29. T.J. Hockenson at $1 after $8. Travis Kelce at $6 after $14. Keenan Allen at $1. Eight dollar players in total, and if even three of them do anything this roster is dangerous.

And then there is Parker Washington at $21, which is more than he paid for DK Metcalf and three and a half times what he paid for Travis Kelce. It is the single most confident purchase anybody made all night on a player the rest of the room had priced at approximately nothing. One playoff appearance in nine seasons says the boring approach was not working. This is not the boring approach.
Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.best: Alvin Kamara, $1. Twenty-nine dollars last year. One dollar tonight. Somebody had to.
Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.worst: Parker Washington, $21. Three and a half Travis Kelces.

Good Will Hunting.headline: The best two players and then a cliff
body: Ja'Marr Chase $63 and Christian McCaffrey $59 is the strongest pair anybody walked out with, and $122 to own it. Seventy-two percent of his money sits in three players, the most concentrated roster in the league. When it works it is unbeatable and when either man misses a month it looks exactly like 2025, where the five biggest buys in this room finished sixth, fourteenth, 8-20, fourth, and in the Sacco Bowl.

Then Jadarian Price at $22, a rookie running back who cost precisely the same as Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow and Patrick Mahomes combined. Read that again. Three starting quarterbacks, or one man who has not yet been handed a jersey number he will keep. Terry McLaurin at $21 after going $30 last year is genuinely sharp work, and Joe Burrow at $11 is the third-best quarterback value of the night.

After McLaurin it is five dollars and under for ten straight players. This is a lineup that wins six weeks by forty and loses six weeks by forty. In a fourteen-team league with six playoff spots, that is a coin flip in a very expensive coat.
Good Will Hunting.best: Terry McLaurin, $21. Nine dollars off last year for the same production.
Good Will Hunting.worst: Jadarian Price, $22. The exact price of Hurts, Burrow and Mahomes stacked on top of each other.

ShakeNBake.headline: Three studs, two dollars, still no ring
body: Saquon Barkley $52, Ashton Jeanty $43, Nico Collins $43. A hundred and thirty-eight dollars in three men, and all three came in under what this room paid for them last year, which is the correct way to be top-heavy: buy the expensive guys when the market has gone quiet rather than when it is screaming.

The problem starts immediately afterward. Carnell Tate at $13 and Jonathon Brooks at $10 are dart throws being asked to hold down a flex spot on a contender. Mike Evans at $12 is the one honest piece of middle-class value. Trevor Lawrence at $7 is a quarterback bought on vibes. And two dollars went entirely unspent, which in an auction is two dollars set on fire in front of witnesses.

Fifteen seasons, two runner-up finishes, zero rings, and the roster shape that produced both of those near misses is sitting right here again: an elite top, a soft middle, and a season that comes down to whether the third receiver hits. The man who built this website ranked himself ninth on it, which is either integrity or a very long con.
ShakeNBake.best: Mike Evans, $12. He cost $28 in this room a year ago.
ShakeNBake.worst: Two dollars, unspent. In an auction that is not thrift, that is litter.

Mac Daddy.headline: Four receivers, one back, one boat
body: Jonathan Taylor at $62 was a $44 player last year, so he paid eighteen dollars in certainty tax, and then built a genuinely good receiver room behind him: DeVonta Smith $34, Tee Higgins $25, Garrett Wilson $23. A workhorse back and three real receivers is a playoff spine, and he finished fourth last season with considerably less than this.

The second running back is Rico Dowdle at $13, up from $2, and behind him it is Kenny Gainwell at $6 and Tyler Allgeier at $2. In a lineup that starts two backs and two flexes, that is one hamstring away from a season decided by a Tuesday morning waiver claim and a prayer.

George Kittle at $6 after going $22 last year is the best tight end value of the draft. Lamar Jackson at $21 is the exact opposite: the second most expensive quarterback in a league that pays four points for a passing touchdown, bought in a room where two starting quarterbacks changed hands for ten dollars combined. That is not acquiring a player. That is buying a boat and then telling everyone how much you use it.
Mac Daddy.best: George Kittle, $6. Sixteen dollars cheaper than last year at the position nobody solved.
Mac Daddy.worst: Lamar Jackson, $21. One quarterback slot, four-point passing touchdowns, twenty-one dollars.

Kim Jong Nate.headline: Two Ferraris and a bus pass
body: CeeDee Lamb $52 and Justin Jefferson $51 is $103 on two wide receivers, and both came cheaper than last year, so the purchases themselves are perfectly defensible. Add Emeka Egbuka at $25 and Tyler Warren at $17 and he owns the best receiving corps in the league on paper. Then you scroll down to the backfield and the music stops.

The entire running back room cost thirty-four dollars. Quinshon Judkins $23, Jacory Croskey-Merritt $9, Kaleb Johnson $1, Sean Tucker $1. This is a lineup that starts two running backs and two flexes every single week, and he answered that requirement with one real player and three scratch-off tickets. A hundred and thirty-one dollars went to receivers. Thirty-four went to the position that touches the ball on every snap of every drive.
Jayden Daniels at $10 after $21 last year is clean, sensible work. None of it changes the arithmetic. He bought two of the best players in the room and then has to get them to the stadium somehow.
Kim Jong Nate.best: Jayden Daniels, $10. Half of last year's price for the same quarterback.
Kim Jong Nate.worst: The backfield, $34 total. Four running backs for less than his third receiver cost.

Leo the Cleo.headline: Seventy-three dollars on the first name called
body: Jahmyr Gibbs at $73 is the most expensive player in the fifteen-year history of this league. The previous record was $70 for Ja'Marr Chase last season and that team finished sixth. He nominated Gibbs first, bid against a room that was delighted to let him have it, and spent thirty-seven percent of his budget before a single other person had bought a single other player. The auction had been running for about ninety seconds.

Then Josh Allen at $29, the most expensive quarterback of the night in a draft where the entire quarterback market cost $153 across twenty-five bodies. Kyren Williams at $32 and Malik Nabers at $29 are both good buys, genuinely. That is $163 in four men, and after Tony Pollard at $18 the roster drops off a table: nine players at a dollar or two, and a WR2 who cost four dollars.

Six seasons here, zero playoff appearances, a 33-78 record and 4-24 last year. Aggression was absolutely the right instinct and nobody should tell him otherwise. Spending record money in the opening minute and then furnishing nine roster spots from the clearance rack is the single most reliable way this league produces a bad team, and there are fifteen years of receipts one section down.
Leo the Cleo.best: Cooper Kupp, $2. He cost $11 here last year.
Leo the Cleo.worst: Jahmyr Gibbs, $73. A league record, set before anybody else had spent a dollar.

FreeGucci.headline: He turned two hundred dollars into a smoothie
body: Sixteen players. Exactly one of them cost a dollar and not one of them cost more than $44. Chase Brown $44, George Pickens $37, DJ Moore $23, Drake Maye $15, Alec Pierce $14, Michael Pittman $13, Jordan Mason $13, Blake Corum $10. Every single price on this roster is a middling price. There is no star to build around and no bargain to feel clever about. He took $200 and blended it until it was smooth.

Only $147 of it landed in players who will start at an offensive position, thirteenth of fourteen, and five dollars never left his pocket at all. Thirty-one dollars is parked on the bench. Spreading money evenly is a real strategy in a year when the middle of the board is underpriced. This year the middle of the board was the single most expensive part of it, and he bought all of it.

Three championships says he understands something about this league that the rest of us do not. This roster says whatever it is, it did not survive contact with a thirty-seven dollar bid on George Pickens. He owns sixteen players and not one of them is going to be the reason he wins a week.
FreeGucci.best: Zach Charbonnet, $5. Six dollars off last year and a genuine handcuff.
FreeGucci.worst: Alec Pierce, $14. He cost one dollar in this exact room in September.

Hail Mary.headline: The title defense begins with three quarterbacks
body: The defending champion spent twenty-two dollars on three quarterbacks. There is one quarterback slot. He can start one of them. The other two are there for emotional support. In a league that pays four points for a passing touchdown, where Patrick Mahomes went for three dollars, the commissioner assembled a quarterback room and then bought a second kicker to keep it company.

The offensive damage is the real story. His biggest purchase all night was Jameson Williams at $28. Only $142 of his budget reached a starting offensive position, dead last by fifteen dollars, and forty-eight dollars is sitting on his bench, three and a half times the league average. Thirty-eight percent of his money is in his top three players, the flattest roster in the draft by a distance, except this time flat does not mean balanced, it means short.

In 2025 he won this thing by refusing to buy anything expensive, and this site called his draft board the most boring document the league had ever produced. He appears to have filed that as a compliment rather than as a description of a market that happened to be cheap that year. Flat works when the middle is underpriced. Tonight the middle was where all the money was, and he showed up with three quarterbacks and a spare kicker.
Hail Mary.best: TreVeyon Henderson, $13. Fifteen dollars off last year's price.
Hail Mary.worst: The second, third and fourth quarterback. There is one quarterback slot and it has been full since eight o'clock.
